## Open

### T-223 — A microservice process crashes validating a model it cannot call

> _2026-10-05 · core/blong-server · open_

Reproduced without a cluster: run the blong-suite entry with the microservice intent and the dev
database overrides, and the process dies in Registry.start, while the same suite under dev starts.
subject.validation calls every model named by subjectSubjectModelList, and the kustomize realm
answers a model that this process never registers, so the call resolves to undefined and the old
symptom was Cannot read properties of undefined (reading object) raised from a map that named
nothing; the validation now names the model instead. In the cluster the same crash crash-loops the
suite Deployment and fails the migration Job, which is where this was found. Next: make the model
list describe what the process can actually call, or make the validation skip an unanswered model
and say which one it skipped. The dev intent loads the kustomize meta folder and microservice does
not, so the two differ in what exists at validation time.

### T-276 — Guard that subject.validation derives the CRUD validations

> _2026-10-08 · core/blong-server · open_

Nothing asserts that `subject.validation` derives the CRUD validations for the public models, and
the failure is silent in both directions: reading the wrong place published no validations at all
and every test still passed, and the deployed suite served requests without validating them while
`scripts/k3d-e2e.sh` passed. A guard needs a suite that loads `srv` with a public model plus a way
to read the gateway routes: `Gateway.describe()` is public and a tap entry such as
`test/framework/index.test.ts`, which loads the registry directly, can reach the port through
`registry.ports`. `test/framework` does not load `blong-server`, so the guard belongs to a package
that does or to a new one.

On probing a deployed suite from outside, which is the cheap way to see the same thing: a missing
validation and a working one both answer through the same route, so only a request the _schema_
refuses distinguishes them. An empty params object is valid for a reference model (a role was
created with an auto-generated name), an unknown property is stripped rather than refused, and those
two probes prove nothing. A wrong _type_ does: `{"role":{"roleName":12345}}` answered
`Validation failed: must be string`, which no handler would have said.
